claim.why_it_matters: Two index entries merged on one line. The index is informative, but a flattened or merged index entry misattributes page references to the wrong headword.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page (PDF p932, printed index page 908, left column top) shows two lines: 'Constant conditional expression 48' and 'Constant entry 282'. The markdown line 3 reads 'Constant conditional expression 48 Constant entry 282': every word and both page numbers are present, in the printed order, and each number still sits directly after its own headword. The only difference is a lost line break (the following lines use a trailing backslash hard break; this one lacks it and sits alone in its own paragraph). No page reference is attached to the wrong headword, so the claimed misattribution does not occur. This is a line-structure/formatting difference in an informative index that does not change meaning.
